name: aomega-m3-pairing-matrix-from-companion
description: The GGM orthogonality pairing matrix J solved as a linear system A J Abar^T = J from the companion matrix of the descendant operator, calibrated against GGM's printed J at ranks 2 and 3, and applied at rank 6.
verdict: RETRACTED PREMISE. This probe set out to solve A J Abar^T = J for the pairing matrix. That equation does not exist: GGM (92)'s right-hand side carries q^m and its two indices shift in opposite directions (m-1 against -m-1), so the pairing is NOT m-invariant and (93) is an INTEGRALITY statement (Laurent entries, determinant 1) rather than an invariance. What survives is G1, the determinant necessary condition det A * det Abar = 1, which holds for all three knots INCLUDING the pretzel — so Part 1's rank-6 palindromy obstruction does not by itself forbid a pairing, and the two obstructions are separate. A harness bug sat underneath the wrong premise and would have hidden it: linsolve was fed coefficients containing none of the unknowns, so every solution space read as empty. It is deliberately NOT repaired. Superseded original follows. The pairing matrix J is SOLVED FOR, not read off a printed source. W_{m+1} = A_m W_m with A_m the companion matrix, so GGM's orthogonality relation holds for all m iff A J Abar^T = J — LINEAR in J's entries. Its necessary determinant condition det A * det Abar = 1 holds for all three knots INCLUDING the pretzel (G1), so Part 1's rank-6 palindromy obstruction does not by itself forbid a pairing; the two obstructions are separate. Bar conventions on the descendant variable, both run and reported: {'W->1/W': {'4_1': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}, '5_2': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}, 'pretzel': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}}, 'W->W': {'4_1': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}, '5_2': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}, 'pretzel': {'dim': None, 'contains_ggm_J': None}}}. Conventions reproducing GGM's printed J at ranks 2 and 3: NONE; adopted: None. Pretzel solution-space dimension under it: None.
